title: The 1936 paper on computability
summary: Turing introduced the idea of the universal machine and connected computation with formal logic.
significance: This paper laid the conceptual groundwork for modern computing and later AI.

title: Bletchley Park and Enigma
summary: Turing joined the effort to break Enigma messages during the Second World War.
significance: His work helped shorten the war and showed how computation could be used for strategic problem-solving.

title: The Bombe and machine-assisted cryptanalysis
summary: Turing helped design and improve the Bombe, a machine that sped up the search for Enigma settings.
significance: This was an early example of using engineered machines to solve complex reasoning tasks.

title: The ACE design proposal
summary: Turing proposed the Automatic Computing Engine, outlining a programmable machine with broad potential.
significance: It reflected his belief that computers could support general-purpose problem solving beyond arithmetic.

title: The imitation game paper
summary: Turing asked whether machines could think and proposed the imitation game as a test.
significance: This paper became a foundational reference point for debates about machine intelligence and AI.

title: Later life and public persecution
summary: After the criminal conviction and social consequences, Turing's later years were marked by both isolation and scientific influence.
significance: His life illustrates how intellectual achievement and social justice are deeply intertwined.
